players.product: thermal-spray coatings (plasma-resistant and electrostatic chuck coatings) applied to semiconductor and FPD manufacturing equipment parts

quarterly_data.signal: Demand versus the FY ending March 2027 plan (CEO Kazuya Kobayashi, Q&A): semiconductor-related numbers are up considerably now; they fluctuate widely so he is not sure he captures them accurately, but after recalculating in March and April he has a feeling they have already exceeded the plan by about 10%. Director Hiroshi Goto: excluding retirement-benefit and subsidy items the plan assumes higher profit, but the second half was planned conservatively because some semiconductor production equipment makers had yet to announce results; FX assumption about JPY150 to the dollar. CEO: the memory price spike has no direct impact (more equipment sales could raise demand, extent unclear); material price hikes are not factored in - inventory on hand covers demand for the rest of the year, and the company is considering surcharges or case-by-case negotiation. Presentation: semiconductor market expected to remain strong this fiscal year.
quarterly_data.figure: Semiconductor-related numbers already about 10% above plan (CEO's feeling); FX about JPY150 to the dollar

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity and capex (CEO Kazuya Kobayashi, Q&A and presentation): annual capex, typically around JPY4.5 billion, rises to nearly JPY10 billion from 2025 and 2026 and will be kept at JPY9 billion to JPY11 billion a year through the TOCALO 2030 five-year plan; the aim is to double semiconductor-related production capacity (from around a 2024-2025 base), plus investment in aircraft-related and overseas areas. Land: the company is preparing new plant land in the Nagoya area and considering buying adjacent land, and will include land acquisition in the plan if needed, at about JPY10 billion per year. Productivity improvement through automation and high-efficiency booths is essential as Japan's working population declines.
quarterly_data.figure: Capex JPY9 billion to JPY11 billion a year (historically around JPY4.5 billion); semiconductor capacity to double

quarterly_data.signal: Customers and strategy (CEO Kazuya Kobayashi, Q&A and presentation): Tocalo works with semiconductor manufacturing equipment makers - globally the main players are two companies in the US and two in Japan, and it does business with several of them, so its operations are skewed toward the US and Japan; its service bases in Taiwan and China do not produce large numbers. The TOCALO 2030 semiconductor figures add up forecasts for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2031 received from each customer, and include a small amount from new approaches - to a US company in fields other than etching and to equipment makers in areas such as exposure systems. Plan: aggressive capex, advanced thin-film technologies (PVD, CVD), entry into equipment other than etching such as exposure equipment, and a stronger recoating business; new technologies include PVD / CVD films and engineered surface microstructures (such as 1-micron or 5-micron height unevenness) for exposure systems, coatings on ceramics and specialized materials, and additive manufacturing (laser cladding) that could lead to integrated part-making plus coating. Overseas expansion beyond China, Taiwan and the US is being considered in ASEAN (Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore), and the Indian market over the medium to long term.
quarterly_data.figure: Main semiconductor equipment players: two companies in the US and two in Japan

quarterly_data.signal: Constraints (CEO Kazuya Kobayashi, Q&A): the lull at overseas subsidiaries reflects restrictions on selling the latest technology in China - Tocalo's overseas development does not include the latest technology and next-generation requirements are expected to impose further restrictions, so the latest technologies are not included in the medium-term plan, which is set with some restraint given the US-China and US-Japan lines on innovative technology. In industrial machinery the company had expected significant growth from NAS batteries, but a withdrawal from that business was announced last year, so it must look for new-energy alternatives and expects this fiscal year to be much the same as last. The TOCALO 2030 ordinary margin target (around 22.2%, versus the current 23%) is set cautiously given aggressive investment in people and equipment, with possible further heavy equipment investment in the fourth or fifth year.
